rationale: The target, H-1, SG-1 and FR-7 establish required versus performed braking as what must be characterised, so including braking-response state is justified. However, the declared scope also incorporates obstacle detection and perception information into P. FR-7.2, FR-7.2.4 and the architecture establish supporting perception functions, but their contribution to braking decisions does not establish those functions themselves as part of the braking-omission phenomenon. FR-7.1's detection-based trigger likewise does not independently justify including detection behaviour.
determining_elements: “Braking-maneuver decision and execution state” legitimately focuses on the system's required braking response; system behaviour alone is not grounds for overextension.
The scope explicitly includes “obstacle detection,” extending P to an observation function rather than treating obstacle presence and proximity as conditions under which braking is required.

“Distance-to-obstacle information,” grouped with detection, further brings supporting perception information into scope; physical obstacle distance can inform whether braking is required without making its determination part of P.
